value: Four-way interactions involving group, peer feedback, peer value, and energy intake were observed in bilateral fusiform face area.
For LOC+, greater FFA activity during negative, relative to positive, feedback from high-value peers was positively associated with overall energy intake during the subsequent test meal.
For LOC−, FFA activity during peer feedback did not relate to subsequent energy intake.

Heightened engagement of FFA may reflect a bias towards processing negative feedback from high-value peers, and this bias was positively associated with consumption during the test meal in girls with LOC eating.

model_representation_notes.value: Energy intake was modeled as a continuous mean-centered regressor in the four-way interaction; follow-up associations were reported separately by group and task condition.
